_note: Chapter quiz questions shown in the app. The right answers live only on the server (functions/learn.py); scripts/learn_test.py checks the two match.

opts: A loan you give to a bank
A small piece of a company
basics.why: A share is a small piece of a company. Own a share of Apple and you own a sliver of Apple.

basics.q: You buy 5 shares at $20. The price rises to $24. What is your profit?
basics.why: Each share went up $4, and you have 5 of them: 5 × $4 = $20.

opts: Buys more shares when the price falls
Sells for you if the price falls to the level you picked
basics.why: A stop-loss is your safety net: it sells when the price falls to your level, so one bad trade can’t hurt too much.

basics.q: A red candle on a chart means…
opts: The price closed higher than it opened
The price closed lower than it opened
basics.why: Red means the price ended that period lower than it started. Green means it ended higher.

basics.q: Who wins a battle with friends?
opts: Whoever grows their account by the biggest %
basics.why: Everyone starts with the same virtual cash. The biggest % gain wins, no matter how many trades.

charts.q: You see a big drop on a 5-minute chart. What should you check first?
opts: The daily chart, to see the bigger picture
charts.why: Zoom out first. A scary drop on a short chart can be a small dip in a bigger uptrend.

charts.q: Higher highs and higher lows mean…
charts.why: Each high and each low is above the one before it: buyers are in control. That’s an uptrend.

charts.q: A stock keeps getting stuck under $50. $50 is…
charts.why: A price it keeps failing to get above is a ceiling: resistance.

charts.q: A price jumps on very low volume. That move is…
opts: Weaker: few traders are behind it
charts.why: Low volume means few people took part, so the move can fade fast. Big moves on big volume are more believable.

charts.q: RSI drops below 30. That means the stock…
opts: Has dropped fast and may be oversold
Has no buyers left at all
charts.why: Below 30 is oversold: it fell fast, so a bounce is more likely, but never certain.
